legend: Table S1. Quality control, read processing and gene-space coverage. Sheet S1: per lesion, the barcodes at each quality-control stage (raw, QC pass, singlets; Figure S1), the median genes and UMIs per cell and the median mitochondrial fraction; the reads processed and pseudoaligned for each validation run; and the coverage of the compartment marker panel and of each programme gene set in each cohort’s gene space before and after the symbol-mapping correction. Sheet S1b_validation_chemistry: verification of the chemistry of the validation runs from read structure (base composition by read-1 position, inclusion-list matches of the 5,000 most frequent barcodes, and UMI recovery under v2 and v3 settings).

Table S2. Programme gene sets and the full transcription-factor screen. The six programme gene sets (sizes and members); for each of the 730 TFs and each programme, the per-lesion and pooled depth-controlled Spearman ρ with the leak-free programme score in the discovery cohort, the number of lesions with the same sign, the rank within programme and the candidate status, unrounded; the corresponding validation values for the 717 TFs evaluable in the validation gene space; and the reproduction counts of the candidates of all six programmes in the validation cohort (Figures 3E and S8A). Added after the independent audit: the source of every gene of the six programme sets and of the eight composite components (Reactome pathway or literature addition, and presence in each cohort’s gene space), and the construction of the composite scores (components, weights and the fixed robust SD divisors).

Table S3. Correlation between the inflammatory and tissue-forming scores, per lesion and pooled. Numbers of stromal cells; raw and depth-controlled Spearman ρ for the composite, full and leak-free score definitions (Figures 4A and S5); and Hartigan’s dip test of each score (Figure 4E).

Table S4. Gene-set × scoring-method sensitivity. For the 18 combinations of inflammatory gene set, tissue-forming gene set and scoring method (Figure S3): raw and depth-controlled ρ between the two scores and retained dispersion, pooled and per lesion.

Table S5. Stromal-set definition, integration method and state labelling. Harmony-corrected versus uncorrected embedding (stromal set sizes and overlap, TF screen agreement; Figure S2); the marker-defined stromal set (cell numbers, enrichment, coupling and retained dispersion); the sign of each candidate’s pooled ρ in the cluster-defined and marker-defined sets, per TF and summarized as counts for the six programmes and for the two main programmes; the per-lesion stromal share, top-decile share and enrichment of the primary analysis (Figure 2B) and the corresponding sensitivity series with the decile ranked on the leak-free score; and the validation state labels defined within the cohort versus projected from the discovery cohort (proportions, agreement and confusion; Figure S7).

Table S6. Deposited matrices versus requantification (discovery cohort). Per lesion and pooled: barcode and UMI recovery, enrichment fold, stromal set sizes and Jaccard overlap, pooled correlations, retained dispersion and candidate agreement for the deposited matrices, for the requantification of all barcodes and for the requantification restricted to matrix barcodes (Figure S4).

Table S7. Receptor expression by stromal state. Pseudobulk expression (log₂ CPM) of ten inflammatory-ligand receptors in inflammatory-state and tissue-forming-state stromal cells, per lesion and pooled, with the per-lesion difference and the percentage of cells expressing each receptor (Figure 5A, B); and the cell-level linear mixed model with lesion as a random effect.

Table S8. Compartment composition and coupling by compartment. Per lesion and pooled: cells per compartment and per fine cell type (number and percentage of all cells; Figure 1E), under the adopted annotation, the earlier annotation version and the rejected cell-majority scheme (Methods); the share of each compartment among all cells and in the top decile of the tissue-forming score, with fold enrichment and permutation p (10,000 permutations; Figure 2B); and the depth-controlled ρ between the two programmes within each compartment and between the myeloid M1 and M2/repair axes (Figure 6). Added after the independent audit: the raw and depth-controlled correlation between the composite inflammatory and tissue-forming scores within each compartment of both cohorts, per lesion and pooled.

Table S9. Gingival stromal cells of GSE164241. Per donor (13 healthy, 8 periodontitis, 1 periodontitis with leukocyte adhesion deficiency 1) and pooled: cell numbers, depth-controlled ρ between the two programmes (Figure 7A), and the sign of each discovery candidate’s association for the two main programmes and for the four remaining programmes (Figures 7B and S8B).

Table S10. Co-activity of TF sets and state proportions. The definition of the NF-κB family and osteoblast-lineage TF sets (fixed lists intersected with the candidate lists) and its comparison with the previously used set; per lesion and pooled, Spearman ρ between the mean activities of the two sets, with and without SMAD3 and with the alternative inflammatory set (ATF1 and MTA1 in place of RELA and NFKB1); cross-side TF pairs and the regulon overlap between set members (Jaccard); the factor-by-factor correlation matrix (Figure 5D); Hartigan’s dip test of each set mean; the correlation of MYC activity with each set; the proportions of inflammatory, intermediate, tissue-forming and other stromal cells per lesion (Figure 4C); and a note on the PC1 variance ratio.

Table S11. Analyses added after the independent audit. The random factor-set null for candidate reproduction (1,000 sets of 20 non-candidate factors; sign agreement, median |ρ| and top-20 Jaccard with their p values; Figure 3E); candidate reproduction after removal of programme genes from each regulon (regulon sizes before and after removal, and the factors omitted); and, for retained dispersion, the per-lesion values (SD ratio and variance ratio; Figure 4B), the bin definition, the permutation null (200 permutations; 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles and p), the null reference (matching on the mean activity of ten TFs unrelated to the tissue-forming programme, chosen per cohort), the floor (matching on the tissue-forming score itself), the retained dispersion after matching on the inflammatory score, and the variance reduction per lesion (Figure 4B). In addition, the retained dispersion recomputed with the tissue-forming score residualized on sequencing depth, per lesion, for matching on RELA, on the unrelated factors, on the inflammatory score and on the tissue-forming score itself.

Table S12. Donor origin and provenance of reported values. The sex-marker check of single-donor origin for every sample (XIST against RPS4Y1, DDX3Y, UTY and KDM5D; counts and fractions of expressing cells); and, for every value reported in the manuscript, the script, output file, cell set and score definition from which it was taken.
